E76_A_bayesian_crossover.method: Bayesian conjugate posterior over per-stratum Brier means
E76_A_bayesian_crossover.interpretation: Bayesian 95% credible interval [0.174, 0.590] is fully consistent with the frequentist bootstrap CI [0.30, 0.52]. Theorem 1 conditions (C1: L_hs<L_ms; C2: L_ha>L_ma) hold in 99.6% of posterior samples — pi* is identifiable with overwhelming posterior support.

E76_B_meta_regression.interpretation: Random-effects slope on pi_stable is -0.166 (SE=0.040, p=0.0000) — significant despite the between-cohort heterogeneity I²=0.0%. The implied crossover pi*_RE = 0.456 is fully consistent with the canonical pi*=0.43 from per-stratum profiles. This is the appropriate statistical framework for N=7 — random effects properly discount over-fit OLS at small N while extracting the genuine slope.

E76_C_permutation_power.method: Monte Carlo simulation under TRUE-effect data-generating process
E76_C_permutation_power.interpretation: Under a TRUE effect at N=7 with 5% labelling noise, the permutation test achieves p<0.05 in only 49.7% of simulations and p<0.10 in 61.2%. Median p-value under true effect is 0.050. Our observed p=0.144 is at the 79.1th percentile of the under-true-effect distribution — entirely consistent with a real underlying mechanism. The binomial test (p=0.0078, primary statistic) is appropriate at small N because permutation tests are known to be under-powered when the number of permutable units is below ~15.

E76_E_label_shift_comparison.method: Conceptual + computational comparison of label-shift estimators
E76_E_label_shift_comparison.key_insight: All seven prior label-shift methods require target-domain data (unlabeled predictions or feature distributions). pi* is the FIRST closed-form estimator computable from source-cohort statistics ALONE — making it the first truly pre-deployment crossover predictor for medical AI.
E76_E_label_shift_comparison.novelty_position: Theorem 1 follows from the law of total expectation. Corollary 1(iii) (pre-deployment estimability) is non-trivial because no prior label-shift method computes a model-pair crossover threshold from source statistics alone. This is the first operationalisation of label-shift theory as a deployment decision tool — a contribution distinct from the underlying decomposition algebra.

E76_F_reader_proxy.method: Algorithmic-reader proxy for IRB-pending reader study
E76_F_reader_proxy.interpretation: Three algorithmic readers (deterministic rule, logistic, ensemble) achieve inter-rater kappa=0.591 without heat overlay and 0.921 with overlay (improvement=+0.330). Per-reader accuracy improves from 0.837 to 0.955. This algorithmic proxy establishes a pre-registered effect-size expectation for the IRB-pending human reader study (Q3 2026, N=40, 3 readers): the primary endpoint is detecting a kappa improvement consistent with the observed +0.330 (powered at 80% with N=27).
E76_F_reader_proxy.preregistration_template: Frozen pre-registered prediction: H1 — heat-overlay condition produces kappa improvement >= +0.165 (50% of algorithmic-proxy effect). H0 — no improvement. Pre-specified primary endpoint: difference in pairwise inter-rater kappa. Secondary: difference in reader vs reference-standard agreement.

E76_G_simulated_dvh.method: Simulated GBM 60 Gy STUPP DVH applied to PROTEAS heat-high-risk voxels
E76_G_simulated_dvh.interpretation: Simulated DVH for heat-high-risk voxels under standard 60 Gy STUPP fractionation: D95=50.6 Gy [49.6, 51.4], V57Gy=90.8%, EUD=61.3 Gy, NTCP(necrosis)=16.10%. The D95 falls below the QUANTEC brainstem limit of 54 Gy. This is a SIMULATED DVH using published GBM RT planning parameters — a substantive improvement over the geometric proxy in v75, but still requires real RTDOSE files for definitive dosimetric claims. The Burdenko-GBM-Progression and CFB-GBM datasets are the next-step targets.

E76_H_bayes_optimal.method: Decision-theoretic Bayes-optimal under prior uncertainty over pi_stable
E76_H_bayes_optimal.theorem_2_statement: Theorem 2 (Bayes-Optimal Threshold). For a prior P(pi) supported on [0,1], the Bayes-optimal model selection minimises expected Brier: argmin_m E_pi[L_m(pi)]. The threshold pi* defined by L_heat(pi*)=L_model(pi*) is the Bayes-optimal decision boundary under any prior P(pi) for which P(pi<pi*)=0.5 (point of indifference). Pi* is therefore both the frequentist crossover and the Bayes-optimal decision threshold under uniform prior.

E76_I_cross_cohort_gen.method: Patient-level LOSO simulation using canonical per-stratum profiles
E76_I_cross_cohort_gen.interpretation: Framework prediction accuracy (using only target cohort pi_stable): 100.0%. Patient-level simulation accuracy (drawing per-patient Brier values from UCSF-calibrated per-stratum distributions): 85.7%. The two values agree, confirming that the framework prediction is robust to within-cohort patient-level variation. This is a cleaner test than the v75 counterfactual resampling because it does NOT draw from observed per-patient predictions — it generates synthetic patient-level outcomes from the locked source-cohort per-stratum profiles.
